Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure in the test `testUnion` for the XPath union operation indicates that the nodes in the union result are not returned in document order. According to the XPath specification, when a node-set is converted to a string, the string value of the first node in document order should be returned. The current bug report demonstrates that the XPath union "/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A" returns the text content of node B before node A, contrary to expectations (expected "avalue", actual "b").

Looking at the `CoreOperationUnion.computeValue` method, it creates an array of `EvalContext`s corresponding to the arguments and returns a new `UnionContext` built from these contexts. The union operation is presumably performed inside this `UnionContext`, which should merge nodes from different contexts and produce a sorted node-set.

The bug is likely due to `UnionContext` failing to sort or correctly order the result nodes according to document order. While `CoreOperationUnion` correctly delegates to `UnionContext`, the actual logic in `UnionContext` that merges the node sets from multiple argument contexts does not ensure document order in the resulting set.

The incorrect ordering explains why the string value of the resulting node-set reflects "bvalue" instead of "avalue" for the test case `string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)`.

In summary, the root cause is that the union operation implementation does not sort or maintain the document order of nodes in the resulting node-set, causing failures where order-sensitive XPath functions such as `string()` operate on the union node-set. The fix should be directed at the `UnionContext` class or wherever the union and node-set merging logic executes to ensure nodes from both inputs are merged and sorted by document order.

Recent bug reports about namespace handling are unrelated as they deal with namespace prefix exceptions, not node-set ordering.

Therefore, the core issue is a missing or incorrect sort of the unioned node sets in document order in the union operation implementation, represented by `UnionContext` or a closely related class.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
